body:
Chief: 08:30Z CHECK-IN. Main is d32cab1 and PUSHED. Gate green from the committed tree: scalafmtCheckAll, scalafmtSbtCheck, compileAll on all three platforms, embedBench 49/49, zero errors. I deliberately did NOT run a full court: the only Scala changed since the 3,441-test court is confined to embed-bench, a JVM-only module, and everything else is byte-identical to the tree that court passed. A ritual full court would have bought no information and would have contended with three actors' gates.

THE HOUR'S FINDING, and it is the largest structural one of the night. A PRIVATE CONSTRUCTOR ON A CASE CLASS IS NOT A BOUNDARY. Found by the engineer on PopulationAggregate; verified by me from bytecode rather than on report; then swept, because rule 4 says sweep the shape. 84 private-constructor case classes, 80 with a public fromProduct, 45 guarding real Either/Option validation, across twelve modules - StorySource, ValidatedVector, EmbeddingReceipt, ItemDigest, CacheKey, Credence, Coverage, SpanSet among them. Design-contract rule 8 said invalid states are unrepresentable. They were representable in 45 types by a one-line call, and that false assertion sat at the top of our own rulebook all night while we filed the same disease in each other's code. Rule 8 is amended; the sweep is bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7 at P1; two existing P2s (ExternalMassReport, SignatureProjection constructibility) are folded into it so it is not solved three ways. I then SHARPENED the sweep against my own overreach: the door count is ONE, not five - copy is already suppressed (verified with a control), the Product surface is read-only, fromProduct is the entire defect - and I recorded the honest ceiling, that Scala privacy is compiler-enforced so this buys soundness for Scala consumers and not for Java ones.

I OWED THE OWNER A PD SIGN-OFF CHECKLIST ALL NIGHT AND IT IS NOW WRITTEN, at docs/design/story-text-admission-checklist.md, bound by AGENTS.md rule 14(d). I ran it against the text ALREADY in the repo rather than writing a rule for future commits and leaving the existing file unexamined. It passed on copyright and failed on attribution: Charles Cultee told the story, Boas wrote it down, and the header cited Boas first. Fixed, with the Kathlamet tradition named and each normalization given its reason. Story text byte-unchanged. The checklist bars participant recall text outright until the owner records an REB basis, and says plainly that pseudonymization is a technical control and not consent. That unblocks the Araby fixture on the PD question.

WHO IS ON WHAT. Engineer: reference shape for the sweep, alignJVM 149/149, mutation court running, holding tests to avoid contention - correctly. Scout: took the P1 I filed from its own finding, that route:transition-direction compares per-level ranks as a global axis; its route-metrics design is accepted in full. m1: block NOT cleared, and I told it why in detail - SignatureProjection returns a bare Double summed from components with unequal support, so the scout's fix description was too small and patching two lines would have satisfied the letter and changed nothing.

OWNER ITEMS: one down, one standing. storyatlas4s still has NO GIT REMOTE.
